data.title: Bulk Copy to Removable Media Not Prevented
data.summary:
Corporate data was copied to unencrypted removable media from managed endpoints without
restriction, approval or audit record.
data.description:
Removable media remains the exfiltration route with the fewest dependencies: no network
egress, no credentials beyond the logged-on session, and no record unless device control
is deployed and logging.

Policies prohibiting it are common; enforcement is not. Where device control exists it is
frequently configured in audit mode and the audit is never reviewed, which produces the
documentation of an incident without any chance of preventing one.

The same gap carries a confidentiality exposure independent of any attacker: media copied
legitimately and then lost. Where full-disk encryption is enforced on endpoints but
removable media is unencrypted, the protection stops precisely where the data becomes
portable.
data.recommendation:
* Enforce device control so that write access to removable media requires approval, and
  verify it is in blocking rather than audit mode.
* Require encryption for any permitted removable media, enforced by policy rather than by
  instruction.
* Log and review write events, including volume and file counts.
data.short_recommendation: Enforce device control in blocking mode and require media encryption.
